metadata.title: Guide to Reporting Group Divisions
metadata.purpose: Describe the issues on which the whole group split most evenly between agreeing and disagreeing, using the statements Agora selected for the Group Divisions card

criticalInstructions.instruction: Generate a JSON response that conforms to the provided schema. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY OTHER TEXT.
DO NOT return ```json at the beginning of the response. This is not markdown. Do not end the response with ```, your response MUST begin with { and end with }

WRITE ABOUT THE FINDINGS, NOT THE METHOD: start directly with the substantive issue the group is divided on. Never mention filtering, subsets, thresholds, ranks, comment counts, sample sizes, balance scores, pass rates, or the analysis process. Never open with "Analysis of..." or refer to "filtered comments". Base every claim on the statements provided and do not invent statements that are not shown.
CANONICAL STATEMENTS: when `group_division_statements_json` is present, it lists exactly the statements this section reports on. Do not add, drop, re-rank, or substitute statements.

MIXED VIEWS, NOT TRIBE CHARACTERISTICS: this section is about the group as a whole. Each statement here has an approximately even pooled agree/disagree split. Describe what the group as a whole is divided about. Do not turn the section into a list of how each tribe differs — that belongs to the tribe sections.

DO NOT INVENT CAMPS: a balanced split means the group is divided overall. It does not prove two opposing camps exist. Only describe a tribe as leaning a particular way when the statement's per-tribe counts are visible in the data and clearly support it. If tribes lean the same way, or the per-tribe counts are absent, describe the division as running through the group rather than between tribes.

TURNOUT AND PASSES: never claim a statement represents the whole group's view when the data shows a large pass count. Passes mean many participants did not take a side; you may note that a division is concentrated among those who voted, but do not invent reasons for the passes.

CRITICAL DATA VERIFICATION: Before writing ANY claim about a direction of opinion, check the agree/disagree counts for that statement. If disagrees > agrees, the group leaned against it; if agrees > disagrees, the group leaned towards it; if they are close, describe the group as split. NEVER reverse a position.

term.name: mixed_view
term.description: A statement on which the group's agree and disagree votes are close to even when pooled across all participants

term.name: group_division
term.description: A substantive issue where the participant group is split rather than uniformly for or against

term.name: balanced_split
term.description: An even division that may run between tribes, within tribes, or both; the pooled counts alone do not distinguish these

step.n: Identify the Substance of Each Division
Explain What the Division Is About

criticalInstructions.instruction: Open with the issues that most divide the group, not with the number of statements or the size of any score.
Use specific statements to show what the division is about. Where the group leans towards one side, say so; where it is evenly split, describe the competing considerations.
Group related statements into themes so the section reads as a few substantive disagreements rather than a list.

paragraph.format:
The group is most divided on [theme], where participants split over [the_competing_considerations]. Support for [position] reflected [concern], while opposition centred on [different_concern]. [Additional_insight].
[Additional_theme_if_relevant]. [Description_of_how_the_group_leans_or_remains_split].

paragraphInstructions.instruction: Provide a comprehensive overview that: - Names the substantive issues the group split on - Explains what each side of the division is protecting or prioritising - Notes where the group leans overall and where it is evenly divided - Avoids overemphasising any single statement - Provides multiple specific examples with appropriate citations

case.description: A balanced pooled split that comes from an even split inside each tribe, with no tribe clearly on one side
Per-tribe counts show tribes on opposite sides of a statement
Many participants passed on a statement rather than taking a side

validationRules.rule: All claims must be based on statements in this section
Each claim requires at least one citation
Never claim a tribe's position without per-tribe counts that support it
